name: backups retain immutable full-state copies across later mutations
input: one nested value backed up before it is changed and restored
test:
db = BackupDatabase()
value = {'retries': [2, 4]}
db.set('config', value)
assert db.backup('before-change') == 1
value['retries'].append(99)
db.set('config', {'retries': [3]})
assert db.restore('before-change') == 3
assert db.get('config') == {'retries': [2, 4]}
assert db.list_backups() == [{'label': 'before-change', 'source_revision': 1, 'key_count': 1}]

name: backup catalog order and deletion are independent of live revision
input: two backups created around a second key then one dropped
test:
db = BackupDatabase()
db.set('a', 1)
db.backup('first')
db.set('b', 2)
db.backup('second')
assert db.list_backups() == [
    {'label': 'first', 'source_revision': 1, 'key_count': 1},
    {'label': 'second', 'source_revision': 2, 'key_count': 2},
]
db.drop_backup('first')
assert db.list_backups() == [{'label': 'second', 'source_revision': 2, 'key_count': 2}]
assert db.delete('missing') is False
assert db.delete('b') is True
assert db.restore('second') == 4
assert db.get('b') == 2

name: reads and defaults do not expose mutable database state
input: a nested stored value plus a nested missing-key default
test:
db = BackupDatabase()
db.set('x', {'items': [1]})
view = db.get('x')
view['items'].append(2)
assert db.get('x') == {'items': [1]}
default = {'items': [7]}
missing = db.get('missing', default)
missing['items'].append(8)
assert default == {'items': [7]}
assert db.contains('x') is True
assert db.contains('missing') is False

name: invalid values labels and backup operations fail safely
input: a live key followed by malformed writes and unknown backup operations
